resources.string: Saves every text and picture message on this phone to one file, on the phone or Google Drive, in minutes. It can keep that file up to date by itself, as often as every hour, and your computer backup can start from it.
One made here with Back up this phone, or from the extension: Settings → Phone restore → Make the restore file.
With a USB cable, Google Drive, or however you usually move files.
You’ll see what’s in it before anything on the phone changes.
Message Archivist becomes your SMS app while it restores

Android only lets the SMS app add messages. At the end you switch back to Google Messages. Texts that arrive meanwhile are kept, and Google Messages fetches picture messages afterwards. Nothing already on this phone is added twice.

For group chats: a message you received in a group lists everyone it went to, you included, and this phone doesn’t say its own number. Leave it empty to go ahead without it (group messages you received would show as separate chats).
All of it goes into one file you choose where to keep.
The file is bigger, but it’s a complete copy.

Texts, picture messages and group chats, with their exact times. Chat (RCS) messages are in it as Google Messages keeps them on the phone; at the moment it doesn’t keep some you send, so those can be missing.
There are no texts on this phone to back up.
Message Archivist can’t read your texts
To back them up it needs the SMS permission. Allow it in the app’s settings, then try again.
“%1$s” has the %2$s chats saved before you stopped. Back up again for all of them.
%1$s photos or videos couldn’t be read and were left out.

Copy the file to your computer (or keep it on Google Drive), then in the Message Archivist extension for Chrome: Settings → Tools → Bring in a phone backup. From then on the extension keeps it up to date from Google Messages for Web, including chat messages the phone doesn’t keep. To put it back on a phone, open it here.
Pick a backup made before: only what’s new is added, such as today’s messages, or its photos if it was made without them.
%1$s new messages and %2$s photos added to “%3$s”, which now has %4$s messages from %5$s chats (%6$s).
Made without photos: %1$s photos and videos can be added later (Update a backup, with photos on).
Keeps “%1$s” up to date %2$s, in the background, adding only what’s new. Change how often in Settings.
Backing up %1$s to “%2$s”. The first one runs soon.
Your texts aren’t backed up yet
Back this phone up in a few minutes, then keep it up to date by itself.
%1$s messages · %2$s chats · %3$s photos and videos on this phone
Adds what’s new to your backup file, in the background.
Turning it on makes a backup now, then keeps it up to date. Where should it go?
Online (Google Drive or similar): sent whole each time
Android picks the exact time, when the battery isn’t low, and may wait longer to save battery, more so if the app hasn’t been opened for a while.
The file is online, so the whole file is uploaded each time: this often, with photos, can use a lot of data.
Off makes a smaller file; photos can be added later.
Waits until the phone is plugged in.
For a file on Google Drive or another online place, so it doesn’t use mobile data.
A quiet notification with how many messages were added. Problems are always shown.
No internet access: your messages only go where you save the file.
Texts, contacts and notifications, in Android’s settings.
Message Archivist isn’t allowed to read your texts any more. Open it and allow it.
You can leave this screen: it keeps going and shows its progress in a notification.
%1$s messages restored. Restore again to carry on: nothing is added twice.
All %1$s messages were here already, so nothing was added twice.
Make Google Messages your SMS app again, so texts and picture messages work as usual.
Google Messages is your SMS app again.
Message Archivist is still your SMS app
Switch back to Google Messages to send texts and get picture messages.
Message Archivist needs to be your SMS app while it restores. Tap Restore and choose Message Archivist.
Message Archivist isn’t your SMS app, so Android won’t let it add messages.
Restore or backup finished, and texts that arrive during a restore
%1$s messages restored. Switch back to Google Messages to finish.
From %1$s. It’s saved, and shows in Google Messages once that’s your SMS app again.
Google Messages fetches it once it’s your SMS app again. If it doesn’t appear, ask the sender to send it again.
It only puts backups back on this phone. To send texts, make Google Messages your SMS app again.
